Not normal fan stuff—like, I *knew* she was in love with me. The way she adjusted her hair, the way she paused before a line, I read all of it as her trying to tell me, “I see you, I’m yours.” I even thought some of her posts online were coded just for me, even though she doesn’t know my name.

Around the same time, I started hearing… commentary, I guess. It’s usually more than one voice, kind of hanging around the edges of my thoughts. Sometimes they talk about what I’m doing, like, “He’s walking too fast,” or “He’s messing it up.” Other times they say I’m special, or that she really *is* waiting for me. I don’t hear them all day, but often enough that I get thrown off in auditions.

My mood’s been weird too. There are days I feel wired and unstoppable, barely sleeping, thinking this is all building toward some big break. Other days I’m more flat, doubting myself, but the voices and the feeling about her don’t really line up neatly with how my mood is. It’s all kind of blended together, and I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D005-D006_h001.question_a:
I’ve been having these… experiences for about two months now, and they’re really messing with my life. It started with this absolute certainty that this well‑known casting director is in love with me. I’ve only met him briefly at an audition, but I’m convinced he’s sending me secret messages through Instagram posts and the way certain roles get cast, like he’s trying to reach me without being obvious. It feels so real that I’ve shown up near places I think he’ll be, just to “accidentally” run into him.

Around the same time, I began hearing voices. It’s usually a couple of male voices, sort of commenting on what I’m doing or whispering my name when no one’s there. Sometimes they argue about me, sometimes they say I’m special. They’re there most days now, even when my mood feels pretty flat.

There was a short stretch—maybe a week or so—where I felt super wired and on top of the world, barely slept, thought my big break was coming any second. But that passed, and these beliefs and the voices have just kept going, even when my mood dropped back to normal or even kind of low.

About eight weeks ago, I started hearing this woman’s voice, clear as day, like she’s standing right behind me. She comments on what I’m doing, sometimes whispers my name, sometimes tells me how talented and special I am. Around the same time, I became absolutely convinced this casting director I met once is secretly in love with me. I “see” signs everywhere—her posts, movie posters, even subway ads—that I’m sure are coded messages from her. Most of these two months I’ve been on this insane high—sleeping maybe three hours a night, full of energy, talking nonstop, writing screenplays, feeling like I’m destined to be huge. Money’s been flying out of my account on headshots, classes, Ubers, like it doesn’t matter.

I guess the main thing is I’ve felt “different” for about four months now. It started when I became absolutely convinced I’m meant to redesign how the whole internet works—like I’m the only one who can see the “true architecture” behind cloud systems. It doesn’t feel like just confidence; it feels more like… destiny, like big companies and maybe even governments will eventually depend on what’s in my head.

At work, in meetings, I sometimes find myself repeating parts of what other people just said under my breath—almost like I’m echoing them. I don’t even notice right away until someone gives me a weird look. It’s not on purpose; it just slips out.

My mood has been all over the place lately. There are stretches where I barely sleep, but I don’t feel tired. I’m talking faster, jumping between ideas, and taking on too many side projects because they all feel urgent and brilliant. Then it sort of settles down again for a while, but the “special mission” feeling about my abilities and role in tech never really goes away.

I’ve also caught myself repeating people’s words back to them, almost automatically. A coworker will say, “Let’s deploy to production,” and I’ll murmur, “deploy to production” under my breath, like an echo. I know it’s odd, but it just slips out.

A few weeks into all this, I had this short stretch where I barely slept, was working on wild “world‑changing” designs all night, talking faster than usual, feeling on top of the world. That only lasted maybe a week or so, but even after that ended and my energy went back to normal, the beliefs about my special role and the echoing of people’s speech never really went away.

I keep having this sense that people are watching me, like the airline or security has some kind of file on me, or there are cameras on me specifically. When I walk through the terminal I feel like certain passengers are planted there to observe what I’m doing, or that the crew group chats are really about me. I know it sounds odd, but it feels very real in the moment.

On flights, I catch myself sitting in these really stiff positions and holding them for way too long, like I’ll stand in the galley with my arm out or my head tilted and just stay that way until someone says something. It’s like my body gets stuck.

At the same time, I’ve had these bursts where I barely sleep, feel unusually energetic and chatty, and start planning all these big projects—like changing bases, starting a side business—then it fizzles out. I can’t tell how much those “up” times overlap with the other stuff; it all kind of blends together.

On layovers, I’m convinced the hotel staff and even passengers from earlier flights are involved somehow, like they’re reporting on me to someone. When I walk through the airport, I’m sure the security cameras are following just me, and that crew scheduling is monitoring my every move, not just for work but to hurt my reputation.

On flights, I sometimes find myself holding my body in these stiff, strange positions for long stretches—like standing in the galley with my arm held a certain way or sitting bolt upright and not moving, because I feel like if I move, something bad will happen or “they” will notice. There was a week or two when I felt almost too good—hardly slept, talked a mile a minute, felt unusually confident—then that passed. But the feeling of being watched and the odd posturing never really went away; they’ve been there pretty steadily the whole time.

At the same time, I became convinced management and airport security were watching me. I “knew” there were cameras aimed at me specifically, that our group chat was being monitored. I’d stand in these stiff, odd positions in my hotel room or galley because I felt like I had to hold the “right” pose so they couldn’t read my mind or get to me. It felt purposeful, not like a tic.

For most of these months I’ve been in that revved-up, overconfident state, but there was a stretch of a couple weeks when the high mood dropped and I just felt flat and exhausted—yet the certainty that I was being tracked and observed didn’t let up at all. That part never really goes away.

I’ve been on the rescue team for over a decade, so I’m used to stress, but the last four months have been different. I started getting this fixed idea that my wife is sneaking around on me. There’s nothing concrete—no messages, no weird calls—but if she’s five minutes late or laughs at a text, my mind just locks onto it. I’ve checked her phone, driven past her work, even circled the block a few times on my way home to see if anyone’s parked outside. I know it sounds excessive, but it feels absolutely certain in the moment.

My crew has noticed I’ve been “off.” I catch myself doing these odd little routines, like tapping my helmet exactly three times before getting on the truck or making these exaggerated hand movements when I talk, almost like I’m acting things out. It’s not on purpose; it just happens and then I feel embarrassed.

On some days, I’ve got this rush of energy—sleep a few hours, feel wired, talk more than usual, take extra shifts, feel like I can handle anything. Other days are more flat. I can’t really say how often that “amped up” feeling happens compared to everything else—it comes and goes, and it’s all kind of blurred together over these months.
D005-D006_h013.question_a:
For about four months now, I’ve been absolutely convinced my wife is seeing someone else. It’s not like I caught her texting anyone or anything concrete, but every little thing feels like proof—if she’s five minutes late from work, if she changes her shampoo, I’m sure it’s for this other guy. I’ve checked her phone, driven past her office on my days off, even looked for hidden cameras at home. I know it sounds over the top, but it feels completely real in the moment.

My crew has noticed I move in these odd, kind of ritualized ways—like before a call, I have to tap my helmet three times and circle the truck a certain way, or I won’t get in. Even at home, I’ll open and close doors with this exaggerated, careful motion, like there’s some special sequence I have to follow.

A few weeks back I had this burst of energy for maybe four or five days—sleeping just a couple hours, talking fast, feeling unusually confident, planning big projects—but that passed, and these suspicions and strange habits have just kept going the whole time.
D005-D006_h013.question_b:

It started with this absolute certainty that my wife is cheating on me. There’s no real proof—she shows me her phone, she’s home when she says she is—but I can’t shake the idea. I check her location, reread texts, drive past places I think she might be meeting someone. I know it sounds irrational, but it feels 100% real.

Around the same time, I got what my crew calls “amped.” For most of these last few months I’ve barely slept, maybe three hours a night, but I feel wired, like I’m running on jet fuel. I talk nonstop at the station, jumping from training ideas to plans to overhaul the whole department. I started doing these exaggerated salutes and dramatic hand motions when I talk—almost like I’m acting out a movie scene—and I can’t seem to stop even when people stare.

There was a stretch, maybe two, three weeks, when that high energy dropped off and I felt more flat, but the thoughts about my wife cheating and the weird, overdone gestures stayed just as strong.
